Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:for_loop->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterLoopHeader | wrong rule: Puts a ; right after for (...) or while (...). | right rule: A ; right after the loop header is a null (empty) loop body, so the statements written after it are not repeated by the loop. | | err:for_loop->WrongIterationCount | wrong rule: Updates the loop counter so that the loop runs the wrong number of times. | right rule: The init, test and update together decide the number of passes; trace them to check the count. | | mis:for_loop->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:for_loop->FalseLoopRepeatsNextCode | wrong rule: A loop is an iterative if-else: while the condition is true the body repeats, and when it is false the code after the loop repeats. | right rule: Only the body is repeated; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:for_loop->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:for_loop->ForIsConditional | wrong rule: The body of a for statement executes at most once. | right rule: The body of a for statement runs once for every pass on which the condition is true, which can be many times. | | mis:for_loop->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:for_loop->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:for_loop->ForWhileNotInterchangeable | wrong rule: Some loops can only be written with for, others only with while. | right rule: Any for loop can be rewritten as a while loop and vice versa; for just packages init, test and update. | | mis:for_loop->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:for_loop->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:for_loop->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:for_loop->LoopImpliedByOneTest | wrong rule: Testing one case is enough; Java will repeat the test for the other values by itself. | right rule: A statement runs once each time control reaches it; repeating a test for many values needs a loop. | | mis:for_loop->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:for_loop->MissingBraces | wrong rule: Omits braces around a single-statement body of if, for or while. | right rule: Braces are optional for a single-statement body, but using them anyway avoids bugs when statements are added later. | | mis:for_loop->ProgramEndsAfterLoop | wrong rule: When a loop finishes the program ends, so code after the loop never runs. | right rule: When the loop condition becomes false, control continues with the first statement after the loop. | | mis:for_loop->ReturnDoesNotExitLoop | wrong rule: A return inside a loop does not end the loop; it sets a value each pass (the last one is returned) or returns several values. | right rule: When return executes, the method ends at once, so the loop stops on that pass. | | mis:for_loop->SingleIterationInsteadOfLoop | wrong rule: A task that must be repeated is written once, without a loop, as if one pass were enough. | right rule: A step that must happen several times (or an unknown number of times) needs a loop such as while or for; Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:break_statement->BreakEndsProgram | wrong rule: break ends the whole program. | right rule: break ends only the innermost loop (or switch); execution continues after it. | | mis:break_statement->BreakExitsIf | wrong rule: break leaves the if statement it is written in. | right rule: break immediately exits a loop without letting it run to completion, and in a switch it exits the switch body. | | mis:break_statement->BreakIgnored | wrong rule: break has no effect; the loop body just carries on. | right rule: break leaves the innermost loop at once; the rest of the body and later passes do not run. | | mis:break_statement->BreakIsContinue | wrong rule: break starts the next iteration of the loop. | right rule: break exits the loop immediately; continue skips to the next iteration of the loop. |

(here mixing in: "break leaves the if statement it is written in") | | lvl:break_statement@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: Jump statement: break; immediately ends the innermost enclosing while, for, do or switch. | | lvl:break_statement@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: break; may appear only inside a loop or switch. (Spec: JLS §14.15.) | | lvl:break_statement@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: When break executes: the remaining statements of the body are skipped, the for-loop increment and the condition are not evaluated again, and control continues at the first statement after the loop.
